page: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-200s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor based on the x86_64 architecture, clocked at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside instruction support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. Memory capacity stands at 32.0 GB, providing an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware provisioning also bundles 200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one public IPv4 address, with zero dedicated GPU acceleration.

Performance benchmarks reveal notable strengths in single-threaded computation and memory subsystem throughput. In stress-ng single-core tests, the instance ranks in the top 10 percent, complemented by strong top 25 percent marks in single-threaded gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench text processing. Write bandwidth for large memory blocks reaches 113.08 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25 percent, while PassMark memory metrics reflect comparable strength. Conversely, multi-threaded performance is bounded by the four-vCPU ceiling: stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores remain within the middle 50 percent, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the lower 25 percent. In-memory Redis operations show stable middle-tier performance at 10.61 million SET operations per second, whereas PassMark database operations and static web serving throughput register in the bottom quartile.

The hardware allocation delivers dedicated AMD compute with generous memory capacity per vCPU, offering high cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks that do not justify high core counts. The primary tradeoff centers on limited multi-core scaling and subdued network and web-serving throughput compared to higher-tier configurations. The server fits in-memory caching systems, intermediate data transformation pipelines, memory-intensive batch processing, CI/CD compilation tasks, and small-scale memory-optimized database workloads.
description: The Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-200s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance designed for memory-intensive workloads. It is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs running across 2 physical AMD EPYC cores at 2.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage consists of a bundled 200 GB local NVMe SSD, while GPU hardware is omitted. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core CPU execution in stress-ng and top 25 percent performance in single-threaded compression and Geekbench single-core tests. Large-block memory write throughput reaches 113.08 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded metrics and static web throughput remain average to low due to the four-thread boundary. With its high RAM-to-CPU profile and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance delivers strong cost efficiency for workloads prioritizing memory capacity over massive thread parallelism, such as in-memory caching layers, Redis deployments, data preprocessing pipelines, and specialized background workers.
